about: How every SCE engine reduces the value a hybrid <invoke srcexpr> computes
to the stem of the document it names, written out by hand.
W3C SCXML 6.4 lets an expression name the child to start, and
docs/SCE_ACCEPTED_SUBSET.md 2.13 has the build generate one child per
document `sce:candidates` declares, so the runtime has to say which of
them a value names. An expression is free to compute `file:x.scxml`,
`./x.scxml`, an absolute path or a Windows one for the same document, so
the value is reduced to what the build names the generated child by.
One rule, stated once: the text after the last '/' or '\', without a
leading `file:` scheme, without the extension that follows its last '.'.
A '.' that opens the name is a name, not an extension. The build derives
the stem of each declared candidate by the same rule
(`sce_build::model::document_stem`), so a value and the candidate it names
A value that names no document at all (nothing after the last separator)
has the empty stem, which no candidate has.

cases.name: a file: scheme before an absolute path
a file: URL with an empty authority
a leading dot is part of the name
a leading dot and an extension
a stem that looks like a scheme
